notes.summary: The completed valued algebraic closure is algebraically closed in every characteristic. An actual common complete field with any analytic extension is constructed, for function-level use only.
notes.detailedSummary: Compatible norms on finite algebraic extensions define the valued algebraic closure. Successive roots of approximating polynomials prove its completion algebraically closed without separability or spherical completeness. An isometric embedding into an algebraic closure of any analytic extension gives a common complete field. No current transport through this common field is asserted.
notes.text:
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued. The finite-field foundation is BGR, Non-Archimedean Analysis, 3.2.4/2: every finite algebraic extension of a complete non-Archimedean field has a unique extending absolute value and is complete, including inseparable extensions. This foundation is also proved in supplied n701 Section 3.1. Give every finite subfield of an algebraic closure Kbar that norm. Uniqueness makes the norms compatible on intersections and composita, hence defines a norm on Kbar. Its completion C is a field: for a nonzero limit a of a_m, eventually |a_m|=|a|>0, and |a_m^-1-a_j^-1|=|a_m-a_j|/(|a_m||a_j|), so inverses converge. C is complete, contains K isometrically, and remains nontrivially valued.

For algebraic closure, take monic P(T)=T^d+sum_{i<d}a_i T^i in C[T], d>=1, and put R=max(1,max_i|a_i|). Choose monic P_m in Kbar[T] with coefficient errors at most delta_m=2^(-md)R^(-(d-1)). Their coefficients have norm at most R, and every root has norm at most R: a larger root would make the leading term strictly dominant. Choose b_1 a root of P_1. Given a root b_m of P_m, |P_{m+1}(b_m)|<=delta_m R^(d-1)=2^(-md). Factoring P_{m+1} into d linear factors in Kbar, one root b_{m+1} satisfies |b_{m+1}-b_m|<=2^(-m). The ultrametric inequality makes this sequence Cauchy. Its limit b satisfies P(b)=lim P_m(b_m)=0 by coefficient convergence and the uniform root bound. Thus every nonconstant polynomial has a root, after division by its leading coefficient, and C is algebraically closed. Repeated roots and positive characteristic cause no exception.

For any analytic extension L/K, embed Kbar into an algebraic closure Lbar over K. A maximal partial embedding extends by choosing a root of a minimal polynomial whenever an algebraic element remains, so it is defined on all Kbar. Unique extending norms on finite K-subfields make it isometric. With F=completion(Lbar), this embedding extends isometrically C->F; L also embeds isometrically, agreeing on K. This constructs an actual common complete nontrivially valued field. It does not assert that C completed-tensor_K L is a field. Its use in the integration concerns already subharmonic or harmonic functions, never arbitrary continuous-current pullback.

These proofs appear as Lemmas 1 and 2 in P06.2-argument.md. Rerun the deliverable with bash reproduce.sh. These are mathematical arguments, not conclusions from finite diagnostics.

notes.summary: The integration proves arbitrary-field zero-Hessian recognition on every good separated strict boundaryless pure analytic curve, including imperfect fields, singularities and nilpotents. All field and curve-map quantifiers are retained; arbitrary-dimensional P06.2 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Apply n701 to the completed valued algebraic closure, preserving actual pure-curve geometry, ordinary compact tests and Artinian calibrations. Apply n700 intrinsic recognition upstairs, then published GR Proposition 3.14(6) to descend recognized harmonicity. GR 4.1.2 supplies classical pluriharmonicity with every analytic-extension and curve-map quantifier. Exact GR 3.15 and GJR hypotheses also give G-local real PL and GJR harmonicity. This is a complete new integration draft in dimension one, not an independently reviewed solution of the full atom or an ordinary smooth approximation theorem.
notes.text:
Theorem. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, and let X be an actual good separated strict boundaryless pure one-dimensional K-analytic space. Every finite continuous h:X->R satisfying D[h]=d'd''[h]=0 against all ordinary compact smooth scalar tests, with canonical CLD integration retaining all actual generic Artinian lengths, is GR-harmonic and classically pluriharmonic. It is G-locally real PL and GJR-harmonic. The theorem includes imperfect and positive-characteristic fields, singularities, nilpotents and unequal generic lengths, and holds on every ordinary open.

For every analytic extension L/K, every L-analytic curve Y, and every analytic map f:Y->X_L, the finite continuous composite h o pi_{L/K} o f is GR-harmonic. Here a curve has the published separated, pure dimension-one convention; no additional smoothness, strictness, reducedness, boundarylessness or separability condition is imposed on these test curves or maps. On smooth strict test curves the composite is also Thuillier-harmonic.

Proof. By n1, C=completion(valued algebraic closure K) is an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued analytic extension. Apply n701 Theorems A and B with M=Kbar and n=1. The hypotheses match X and h exactly. They give the actual scalar extension X_C, locally M(A completed-tensor_K C), good separated strict boundaryless and pure one-dimensional, and D[h_C]=0 for h_C=h o pi_{C/K}. No reduction or separability assumption is introduced. The purity conclusion uses n701's componentwise and local proof, rather than total dimension alone. Strict presentations, affinoid neighbourhoods, the base-changed closed diagonal and the relative-interior base-change inclusion supply the other geometric properties. No equality of arbitrary absolute interiors is assumed.

In particular, for every compact ordinary scalar test beta upstairs, n701 supplies a finite embedded E subset Kbar and compact ordinary alpha_E on X_E with beta=q_E^*alpha_E as smooth sections. Its finite-stage transport gives D[h_E]=0. Differentiating the exact smooth-section identity and applying canonical smooth-top-measure projection yields
integral_{X_C} h_C D beta = integral_{X_E} h_E D alpha_E = 0.
The supports remain compact and the continuous multipliers are bounded there. CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2 Proposition 15.3.1 is applied to the differentiated smooth top form. This defines no pullback of an arbitrary continuous current. The all-test descent theorem supplies the indispensable step beyond a direct-image identity.

Calibrations retain the actual lengths. For a finite Artinian H-algebra B of dimension d and a complete extension H'/H, B tensor_H H' is finite-dimensional and already complete. If its local factors are B_j, composition series give d=sum_j length_{B_j}(B_j)[kappa_j:H']. This preserves the moment-degree sums, including inseparable residue degrees, nilpotents and unequal lengths, as used in CLD 13.3.3 and 14.3.6 and n701 Section 10. Scalar top-measure projection has no field-degree factor. The distinct same-carrier finite restriction formula mu_K=[E:K]mu_E in CLD 14.4.3 is not substituted for scalar transport. Generic weights are not divided out.

Now apply n700 Theorem A to X_C over C. Its exact intrinsic recognition scope is every good separated strict boundaryless pure analytic curve over an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field, including singular and nonreduced structures. Hence h_C is GR-harmonic. Its reduction, normalization and puncture-removal gates are part of the supplied supporting proof. No smoothness of normalization over the original imperfect K is assumed. The separate ground-field ambient-probe theorem in n700 is unnecessary.

The published function-level theorem is Gubler–Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025, Proposition 3.14(6): for a k-analytic curve Z, continuous u:Z->R and any analytic extension E/k, u is harmonic if and only if u o pi_{E/k} is harmonic on Z_E. It imposes no smoothness, reducedness, perfectness or algebraicity condition. Apply it with Z=X, u=h and E=C, after upstairs harmonicity has been recognized. All hypotheses hold, so h is GR-harmonic.

The full primary proof of the underlying scalar statement GR 3.5(7), LF lines 827–885, is embedded in P06.2-argument.md. Its descent compares already subharmonic functions on smooth strict probes over a common field. The actual common field for C and any L is constructed in n1. Thuillier Definition 3.1.5 supplies strict-affinoid comparison; Proposition 2.3.18 supplies harmonic-function scalar pullback, with the affinoid harmonic convention and supporting Lemma 2.3.5 retained in full. GR Lemma 2.12 gives boundary projection, and scalar projection is surjective. Thus the boundary inequality upstairs descends by comparison and surjectivity. Finite values eliminate the identically-minus-infinity alternative. No current equation on the common field is used.

By GR Definition 3.13, both h and -h are subharmonic. GR 4.1.2 states exactly that on an analytic curve classical psh equals GR-subharmonicity; its proof uses scalar extension 3.5(7) and forward curve pullback 3.5(8). Apply it to each sign. Definition 4.1 now gives subharmonicity of both signs of h o pi_{L/K} o f for every analytic extension L/K and every analytic curve map f:Y->X_L. Definition 3.13 gives harmonicity of the finite continuous composite. The further extension and smooth-probe quantifiers inside subharmonicity remain intact. Definition 7.1 gives classical pluriharmonicity of h. No equation on X_L or Y is needed, and no arbitrary transcendental-current ascent is claimed.

For the additional regularity conclusion, GR Proposition 3.15 states: a continuous function on any strict analytic curve over a nontrivially valued field is harmonic exactly when it is real PL and every residual class L_h(x) is numerically trivial. Apply it after recognition. GR 2.16 fixes the G-local finite-real-sum convention using logarithms of analytic units on strict domains. GJR arXiv:2111.05741v3, 7 March 2025, field convention 2.2, Definition 5.1, Definition 7.2 and Remark 7.3(1) apply to good strict spaces over complete nontrivially valued fields and identify this residual condition with GJR harmonicity. These hypotheses hold on X. No ordinary CLD-smooth regularity follows.

For an ordinary open Omega subset X, analytic-domain restriction preserves goodness, separatedness, strictness and local dimension; its open inclusion and the boundaryless structural map make it boundaryless (CLD 11.1.7, 11.2.3, 11.4.1 and 11.7.7). Every compact ordinary scalar test on Omega extends smoothly by zero to X: its compact support is closed in Hausdorff X and lies inside Omega, so exterior points have zero neighbourhoods. Differential and canonical-integration domain compatibility restrict the equation (CLD 14.3.5, 15.7.2 and Section 7.7). Applying the preceding proof to Omega proves the every-open assertion.
